summary: Sourcing pass complete on content/blog/how-to-lower-electric-bill-complete-guide.md. Article previously mixed 12¢/kWh math throughout (phantom loads, dryer, wash, LEDs, dishwasher, water-heating, showerhead) — corrected to baseline 17–18¢/kWh where it appears as a load-bearing per-appliance cost.
Article's $115–$180/month average was below EIA's $159.14 mid-2026 / $142.26 FY2024 — corrected to $140–$180 range anchored at ~$159 (mid-2026) and ~$142 (FY2024) with EIA citations.

risks: Frontmatter 'sources:' added as a YAML array — relies on the site's existing frontmatter parser tolerating a multi-line list; if the parser is strict-JSON-only, Hugo/Hugo-equivalent may need adjustment. Existing tags/keywords/categories use array syntax so this should be consistent.

The article mixes RECS site-energy shares (40–50% H/C) and energy.gov utility-bill shares (~30% heating) in different places. The 30% framing wasn't directly invoked in the article body (only the RECS framing was used), so no cross-contamination was introduced; baseline flag remains for future pages.

Step 13 '15–20%' was previously cited as Nest-style learning-thermostat territory; baseline documents Google's ~12% heating / ~15% cooling for Nest. The new ~10% DOE text undercuts the Nest product-box copy in the same article (which still says '12% heating / 15% cooling'). This is a soft inconsistency: the product-box claim is manufacturer-published (allowed by baseline) but it is higher than the DOE scheduling claim. Flagged in the workspace summary for future pass.
Heat-pump and solar table figures were left untouched per packet scope; they are derived ranges rather than single-source claims, so no inline citations were added.
unknowns: Whether the site's frontmatter parser requires quoted list items or accepts the unquoted-dash format used here (existing tags/keywords/categories use bare JSON-array style; the new sources: list uses YAML-style '  - "..."' which matches Hugo's default).

The exact water-heater standby-loss 4–7% figure cited in the Water Heater section — DOE's Home Upgrades page does not give a specific percentage for tank-wrap standby savings; the 4–7% figure is a common DOE range from older Energy Saver materials. Not removed since it's a common rule-of-thumb range, but a stricter pass might want a separate DOE citation for the wrap number.

Original article's 12¢/kWh math was internally consistent across many tables; some derived values (e.g. dishwasher $10–$20/month) were within reasonable range of the 17¢/kWh recompute and were not changed. A future pass could recompute every table to baseline rates.
recommendation: Commander to spot-check frontmatter rendering on a dev build before deploy, especially the new sources: array. After deploy, follow-on pass should (a) align the Nest product-box copy with the new DOE thermostat language or add a manufacturer-source line, (b) recompute remaining derived cost tables (dishwasher, line-dry, fridge-age) to 17–18¢/kWh, (c) add EIA/DOE citations to heat-pump and solar tables for full coverage. The article is now safe to publish as a 'trust-debt payment' flagship: all load-bearing claims either have an inline citation or have been corrected to the verified baseline.
